output.summary: The inflation evidence argues for a hike (hawkish). The deterministic pre-read shows the 12-month anchor roughly a percentage point above the 2.0 goal (gap_pp 1.008), and the September-nowcast gap is even wider (1.113). Momentum readings sit above the goal. The SEP median PCE inflation for 2026 was revised up to 3.7, though the longer-run profile returns to 2.0. Both FOMC statements say "Inflation remains elevated," and two members dissented at the October meeting in favor of a hike. On balance the inflation side is moderately hawkish.

claims.text: The computed 12-month inflation gap is positive, running about a percentage point above target — a hawkish signal.
The stated inflation goal is 2.0, and the anchor sits above it, supporting an argument to tighten.
The September nowcast shows an even wider inflation gap than the headline anchor, reinforcing the hawkish read.
Short-run inflation momentum readings are above the 2.0 goal, arguing for firmer policy.
The committee's SEP median PCE inflation for 2026 is 3.7, well above goal, though it is projected to fall to 2.0 by 2029.
The most recent statement says inflation is still elevated, a hawkish characterization.
Two members dissented at the October meeting, preferring a quarter-point hike, underscoring hawkish pressure.

claims.text: The committee nonetheless held rates and said it would gather more information before acting, a partly offsetting, more patient signal.

Economic activity is expanding at a strong pace. While uncertainty remains elevated owing, in part, to geopolitical developments, domestic spending has been resilient. Inflation remains elevated. The accumulation of more information will help the Committee determine the policy stance appropriate to ensure a timely return of inflation to the Committee's 2 percent goal. The Committee will deliver price stability.
